page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of system memory. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, providing 35433 GB of HDD capacity. The network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing is relatively weak, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance is more robust, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average range, though the overall PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.3xlarge lies in its storage medium and compute profile. While it offers exceptional storage density per instance, the local storage relies on HDD technology rather than NVMe SSDs, which limits random I/O performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a highly economical profile for massive data storage requirements where sequential throughput is prioritized over low-latency random access.

Given these characteristics, the ecs.d1.3xlarge is best suited for workloads requiring large-scale data capacity without demanding high single-core compute performance. Appropriate use cases include MapReduce deployments, distributed file systems like HDFS, large-scale data warehousing, cold storage archiving, and batch log processing.
